newsitem.title: GERMANY: Feed rye offered into German grain intervention.
newsitem.headline: Feed rye offered into German grain intervention.

text.p: Some 34,791 tonnes of feed rye were offered into German grain intervention stores last week after nearly 40,000 tonnes a week earlier, state intervention board BLE data showed.
Free market rye and wheat prices were declining and this supported sales into intervention but free market barley prices were supported by export demand, traders said.
Totals in the November-May 1996/97 season still lag those in the same 95/96 period.
Volumes on Feb 21 totalled 640,556 tonnes compared with 1,434,919 tonnes a year earlier.
The figure described volumes accepted, but not yet delivered to stores, by the close last Friday.
The Feb intervention buying-in price has been set at 241.52 marks a tonne.
